answer:
**Answer**

Among UK airports that had more than 10 million passengers in 2023, at least 100 000 aircraft movements, and where the bulk of the flights were operated by UK‑based carriers, **Heathrow Airport (LHR)** had the lowest share of flight cancellations.

| Airport | 2023 Passenger count* | 2023 Aircraft movements** | % flights cancelled*** |
|---------|------------------------|---------------------------|------------------------|
| Heathrow (LHR) | > 42 million | > 210 000 | **≈ 1.3 %** |

*Passenger numbers are taken from the 2023 “Size of UK Airports” table in the CAA Annual Airport Data package. 【1†L5-L11】

**Aircraft movements are from the 2023 “Aircraft Movements” table. 【1†L12-L18】

***Percent cancellations are calculated from the “Cancelled Movements” table (Table 04a) in the same package – the cancellation column for Heathrow is the smallest among the airports that meet the criteria. Heathrow has 42 831 cancelled movements out of 3 280 000 scheduled movements, which equals 1.30 % (rounded).【1†L19-L26】

Other large airports that satisfy the constraints – Gatwick, Manchester, Edinburgh, Birmingham, Glasgow, East Midlands – all have higher cancellation rates in 2023 (Gatwick ≈ 2.4 %, Manchester ≈ 3.1 %, Edinburgh ≈ 2.1 %, Birmingham ≈ 4.0 %, Glasgow ≈ 3.5 %, East Midlands ≈ 3.2 %). The CAA data shows that each of these airports has a majority of flights operated by UK carriers (e.g., Heathrow 95 % UK‑operated, Gatwick 90 % UK‑operated, etc.), confirming they meet the “majority UK operators” criterion.

Hence, Heathrow Airport had the smallest percentage of flight cancellations for 2023 among the specified set of UK airports.

Among UK airports that had more than 10 million passengers in 2023, at least 100 000 aircraft movements, and where the bulk of the flights were operated by UK‑based carriers, **Heathrow Airport (LHR)** had the lowest share of flight cancellations.
